This article examines the use of epidural anesthesia during open laparotomy, which serves as a supplementary analysis for a specific subpopulation of clinical indicator 8 in [[danmark|Danmark]]. The data highlights significant regional and institutional variations in anesthesia practices across the country during the current reporting period, alongside historical comparisons from the previous two years [^src1].

Nationally, the overall usage rate of epidural anesthesia for this procedure stands at 66.7% in the current year, reflecting a slight increase from 64.7% in 2023/24 and 65.9% in 2022/23 [^src1]. However, this national average masks substantial regional disparities. The [[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland Region i alt]] leads the regions with a 72.9% usage rate, closely followed by the [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]] at 71.5% and the [[syddanmark-region-i-alt|Syddanmark Region i alt]] at 70.8% [^src1]. In stark contrast, the [[sjaelland-region-i-alt|Sjælland Region i alt]] trails significantly at 45.3%, while the [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] sits at 54.4% [^src1].

At the hospital level, [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]] is the top-performing major institution with an 83.3% usage rate [^src1]. [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] (77.9%) and [[herlev-og-gentofte-hospital|Herlev og Gentofte Hospital]] (76.4%) also demonstrate strong adherence to this practice [^src1]. [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] recorded a 100.0% usage rate; however, this is based on a very small sample of just 7 patients, resulting in a wide confidence interval (59.0-100.0) and marking it as a statistical outlier rather than a definitive leader [^src1]. Conversely, the lowest-performing hospital is [[naestved-slagese-og-ringsted-sygehuse|Næstved, Slagelse og Ringsted sygehuse]] at just 32.4%, followed by [[sjaellands-universitetshospital|Sjællands Universitetshospital]] at 46.8% [^src1]. Notably, within the generally high-performing Hovedstaden region, [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] acts as an outlier with a comparatively low rate of 56.4% [^src1].

Trend analysis across the three recorded periods reveals shifting practices at both regional and local levels. While the national average has remained relatively stable, the [[sjaelland-region-i-alt|Sjælland Region i alt]] has experienced a steady decline, dropping from 50.5% in 2022/23 to 45.3% currently [^src1]. The [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]] saw a dip in 2023/24 (63.7%) before rebounding to 71.5% in the current period [^src1]. At the hospital level, [[naestved-slagese-og-ringsted-sygehuse|Næstved, Slagelse og Ringsted sygehuse]] shows a consistent downward trajectory, falling from 37.0% to 32.4% over the three periods, whereas [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] experienced a dramatic, albeit low-volume, surge from 43.8% to 100.0% [^src1].

- "Den samlede 90-dages-mortalitet for indikator 4x i Danmark er 13,0 % (95 % CI: 9,4–17,4) for perioden 01.09.2024 – 31.08.2025" — see [[mortality|Mortality]] ([[danmark|Danmark]]) [^src18]
- "Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg har en 30-dages-mortalitet på 19,2 % (95 % CI: 6,6–39,4) for indikator 4x i perioden 01.09.2024 – 31.08.2025" — see [[mortality|Mortality]] ([[ouh-odense-universitetshospital-odense|OUH Odense Universitetshospital (Odense)]]) [^src18]
- "Herlev og Gentofte Hospital har den laveste 30-dages-mortalitet blandt alle rapporterede hospitaler for indikator 4x i perioden 01.09.2024 – 31.08.2025 med 7,4 % (95 % CI: 0,9–24,3)" — see [[mortality|Mortality]] ([[herlev-og-gentofte-hospital|Herlev og Gentofte Hospital]]) [^src18]
